Revised assessment: The FOMC’s statement conveys a moderately positive outlook—strong labor markets and robust household spending—with inflation near the symmetric 2% objective and risks “roughly balanced.” The decision to raise the target range to 2.25–2.50% aligns with estimated Taylor-type/Clarida-Galí-Gertler policy rules that prescribe gradual tightening as slack diminishes and inflation nears target. Inflation expectations being “little changed” is consistent with inflation-targeting frameworks where expectations anchor the New Keynesian Phillips Curve (Svensson and Woodford) and support price stability. Implementation details—setting interest on reserves at 2.40% and using ON RRP at 2.25%—reflect the floor-system mechanics discussed by Goodfriend (2002), helping keep the effective funds rate within the target range. The noted moderation in business fixed investment tempers the tone: structural IS-curve perspectives emphasize interest sensitivity of investment, while other evidence finds weaker interest-rate elasticity, so tighter policy could exert mixed effects on capex. Term-structure research (Ang and Piazzesi; Rudebusch and Wu) further suggests that the impact on longer-term rates and financial conditions depends on expectations of future policy, reinforcing the Committee’s data-dependent stance and monitoring of global developments. Overall tone: cautiously constructive rather than outright upbeat.
